organizations.normalization_notes: The official memorandum describes a Greco-American trading corporation. No modern successor is inferred.
The COI was the direct institutional predecessor from which the OSS was created in June 1942. It is modeled as a government assignment, not a civilian employer.

affiliations.date_precision: Documented as president on or about November 15, 1941; the source does not state a formal separation date
affiliations.research_notes: A contemporary official memorandum identifies U. L. Amoss as Gramtrade's president when a business associate suggested that he contact COI. Because the memorandum then documents an intervening COI assignment, Gramtrade is the last supported civilian employer before government service, not the immediate pre-OSS affiliation.

affiliations.role_title: Greek political affairs adviser and section organizer
affiliations.date_precision: Approach and Donovan meeting dated approximately November 15-28, 1941; assignment followed; COI became OSS in June 1942
affiliations.research_notes: The official chronology states that Amoss was assigned under the COI Foreign Relations Branch and describes his work. Since COI was the direct predecessor from which OSS was formed, this government assignment is the best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation.

claims.claim_text: A specialist roster may refer to the indexed Vittorio Amoruso in the Italian Operational Group, but the candidate is not yet resolved.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The roster places a Vittorio Amoruso in the Ginny I working party, but it reports a different enlisted grade from the index.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Ambiguous: the exact uncommon name and explicit OSS context align, but the roster supplies no unique identifier and reports Technician Fifth Grade rather than Sergeant.
claims.temporal_assessment: The roster concerns wartime OSS service and supplies no evidence about a pre-OSS affiliation or civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: The candidate is retained for review but is not published as a resolved identity or used in analytics. Box 13 and official Army records are needed.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Uliuss L. Amoss is strongly matched to Ulius Louis Amoss, a wartime OSS director documented in an institutional archival description.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A University of Oregon collection description expands the uncommon name and documents OSS service; a contemporary official memorandum traces U. L. Amoss into COI.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: the rare surname, matching initials, Colonel status in the official chronology, and explicit COI/OSS role align across the NARA index, a direct government record, and an institutional finding aid.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official memorandum provides a dated November 1941 recruitment and assignment chronology; the institutional description independently documents wartime OSS leadership.
claims.match_notes: The profile preserves Uliuss exactly as indexed and adds the independently documented Ulius Louis form as a variant rather than silently correcting the source row.

claims.claim_text: Immediately before OSS, Ulius L. Amoss held a government assignment in the Coordinator of Information's Foreign Relations Branch.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Amoss was assigned to operate under Mr. John Wiley, Chief Foreign Relations Branch C.O.I.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official review states that Amoss was assigned under COI's Foreign Relations Branch and describes his Greek political and recruiting work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity based on the rare name, matching initials and Colonel chronology, NARA index context, and independent institutional OSS description.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate predecessor: the source dates the COI recruitment and assignment from November 1941, before COI became OSS in June 1942.
claims.match_notes: COI is classified as a government assignment and the immediate pre-OSS affiliation, not as a civilian employer.

sources.excerpt_override: Amoss was assigned to operate under Mr. John Wiley, Chief Foreign Relations Branch C.O.I.
On June 13, 1942, the COI became the Office of Strategic Services (OSS).

claims.claim_text: Ulius L. Amoss's last supported civilian employer before his COI assignment was Gramtrade International Corporation, where he was president.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Mr. U.L. Amoss, President of the Gramtrade International Corporation
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official review identifies Amoss as Gramtrade's president when a business associate proposed that he contact COI in November 1941.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity based on the rare name, matching initials, Colonel chronology, official COI record, and independent institutional OSS description.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded: Amoss is identified as president on about November 15, 1941, immediately before the documented COI approach and assignment.
claims.match_notes: Gramtrade is published as the last supported civilian employer before government service. It is not mislabeled as the immediate pre-OSS affiliation because COI intervened.
